newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Friday after Beijing banned state banks from trading on the state debt repo and spot market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 10.00 percent from 9.60 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 5.8 million lots from 4.8 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The central bank announced the ban on Thursday, ordering the banks to stop trading on the state debt market from Friday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down across the board on Friday on sharp liquidity reduction with state banks pulling out of the market on the ban, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell sharply to 121.20 yuan from 122.67 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.6 million lots from 2.2 million lots.
Traders said the ban would continue to hit the spot market in the short term but prices were likely to see a technical rebound early next week.
